hints: Focus on what the size of Kc tells you, a very large Kc means products dominate (right), a very small Kc means reactants dominate (left).
Notice that K3 lies to the right so it must be large, while both K1 and K2 lie well to the left so they must both be very small.
Consider why ammonia dissolves AgCl but not AgI, the complexing pull of ammonia is only enough to overcome the more soluble of the two salts, so compare K1 and K2.
walkthrough:
**Link Kc size to equilibrium position**

Think of Kc as a measure of how far the reaction goes. If it lies to the right, products are favoured and Kc is large (much greater than 1). If it lies to the left, reactants are favoured and Kc is small (much less than 1).

$$K_c = \frac{[\text{products}]}{[\text{reactants}]}$$

**Sort K3 from K1 and K2**

We are told the complex formation lies to the right, so $K_3$ is large. Both dissolutions of $\text{AgCl(s)}$ and $\text{AgI(s)}$ lie well to the left, so $K_1$ and $K_2$ are both very small. This already tells us $K_3$ is the biggest.

**Compare K1 and K2 using ammonia solubility**

$\text{AgCl}$ dissolves in $\text{NH}_3$ because $\text{Ag}^+$ is removed to form $\text{Ag(NH}_3)_2^+$:
$$\text{AgCl(s)} \rightleftharpoons \text{Ag}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{Cl}^-\text{(aq)} \quad K_c = K_1$$
$$\text{Ag}^+\text{(aq)} + 2\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)} \rightleftharpoons \text{Ag(NH}_3)_2^+\text{(aq)} \quad K_c = K_3$$
Removing $\text{Ag}^+$ pulls the first equilibrium to the right. This pull is strong enough to dissolve $\text{AgCl}$ but not $\text{AgI}$, so $\text{AgCl}$ must be the more soluble salt with the larger solubility product. Hence $K_1 > K_2$.

**Combine to give the order**

Putting it together, the large value comes first, then the larger of the two small values:
$$K_3 > K_1 > K_2$$

options.A: Incorrect. This puts the two very small solubility constants above the large complex formation constant. Any equilibrium lying well to the left must have Kc much less than 1, while one lying to the right has Kc much greater than 1.
options.B: Incorrect. This also puts K3 smallest, which is backwards, and it reverses K1 and K2. Since AgCl is dissolved by ammonia but AgI is not, AgCl must have the larger dissolution constant.
options.C: Correct. K3 lies to the right so is large. K1 and K2 lie well to the left so are both small. Because ammonia can pull AgCl into solution but cannot pull AgI into solution, AgCl is more soluble, so K1 > K2. The order is K3 > K1 > K2.
options.D: Incorrect. This correctly puts K3 largest, but reverses K1 and K2. The common trap is to think AgI is more soluble because iodide is larger, but the ammonia experiment proves AgCl dissolves more easily, so K1 > K2.
